card.name: Broken-up spellings leading into "drop"
card.fires_on: Odd word pieces just before an expected "drop" or "dose" ending, such as "eyed" before "rops", "-d" in "multiple-dose" or "dew-drops", and "ird" in "airdrop". Mostly in eye-drop wording.

modes.label: Eye drops split oddly
modes.description: A stray piece such as "eyed" or "e-ard" stands where "eye drops" would be.
modes.example: (a beta-adrenergic blocker)<< eyed>>rops and oral verapamil

modes.label: Hyphen-d in dose containers
modes.description: The "-d" after multiple or single, which starts "dose" in ophthalmic container warnings.
modes.example: use of multiple<<-d>>ose containers of topical ophthalmic products

modes.label: Airdrop or dewdrop
modes.description: A piece inside a compound ending in "drop" in general text.
modes.example: the dew<<-d>>rops which appear in the morning are the

card.writes: It pushes the model to produce "drop" and its forms, such as drops and dropped.
card.plain: It fires on garbled or split spellings where the next piece should be "drop", especially eye drops.
